original_value: This study presents a novel approach for Arabic video text recognition based on recurrent neural networks. In fact, embedded texts in videos represent a rich source of information for indexing and automatically annotating multimedia documents. However, video text recognition is a non‐trivial task due to many challenges like the variability of text patterns and the complexity of backgrounds. In the case of Arabic, the presence of diacritic marks, the cursive nature of the script and the non‐uniform intra/inter word distances, may introduce many additional challenges. The proposed system presents a segmentation‐free method that relies specifically on a multi‐dimensional long short‐term memory coupled with a connectionist temporal classification layer. It is shown that using an efficient pre‐processing step and a compact representation of Arabic character models brings robust performance and yields a low‐error rate than other recently published methods. The authors’ system is trained and evaluated using the public AcTiV‐R dataset under different evaluation protocols. The obtained results are very interesting. They also outperform current state‐of‐the‐art approaches on the public dataset ALIF in terms of recognition rates at both character and line levels.

result.paraphrase: This study introduces a novel recurrent-neural-network-based approach to Arabic video text recognition. Embedded video text is a valuable source for indexing and automatically annotating multimedia documents, yet recognizing it is difficult because of varying text patterns and complex backgrounds. For Arabic, diacritic marks, cursive script, and irregular spacing within and between words add further challenges. The proposed segmentation-free system uses a multi-dimensional long short-term memory network with a connectionist temporal classification layer. It is demonstrated that an efficient preprocessing step together with a compact representation of Arabic character models delivers robust performance and a lower error rate than other recently published methods. The authors train and evaluate the system on the public AcTiV-R dataset under different evaluation protocols. The results are very promising and also outperform current state-of-the-art approaches on the public ALIF dataset in recognition rates at both character and line levels.
